label: talos
description: UWRT Talos AUV, physical plant + navigation sensors + cameras + mechanisms.

keys.what: Every mesh file the pack uses.
The physics: mass, inertia, added mass, damping and buoyancy of the 6-DOF Fossen model.
keys.summary: 34.084 kg, 34.27 L displaced, quadratic damping on 6 axes

keys.what: The frame reported as "the robot's pose" to tasks, TF and placement.
keys.yaml:
# Frame reported as the vehicle pose to tasks, the bridge and placement.
reference_frame: base_link

keys.what: The rigid frame tree, measured from the camera-cage screw (origin). Names the centre of mass.
Meshes the viewer and the simulated cameras draw on the robot.
Boxes that hit the pool walls and the course.
keys.yaml:
# Contact boxes, measured from `origin` like the frames.
collision_boxes:
- {id: hull_0, frame: origin, size_m: [0.35, 0.83, 0.55], center_m: [-0.157, 0.04, 0.022], orientation_wxyz: [1, 0, 0, 0]}
- {id: hull_1, frame: origin, size_m: [0.2, 0.05, 0.05], center_m: [0.073, -0.16, -0.148], orientation_wxyz: [1, 0, 0, 0]}   # poker

keys.what: The eight thrusters in actuator order, each with its delay, lag, slew and force limits.
keys.summary: 8 × lagged_force: delay 0.03 s, rise 0.08 s, fall 0.06 s, ±24 N

keys.what: Kill and arming behaviour: start killed, zero thrust while killed, disarm on kill.
keys.yaml:
# Start killed. Kill clears queued thruster commands and disarms the mechanisms.
safety:
  initially_killed: true
  kill_stops_thrusters: true   # queued commands cleared, realized force coasts down
  commands_while_killed: zero_force   # thruster commands received while killed are zero
  kill_disarms_mechanisms: true
  arming:   # one armed flag shared by these mechanisms
    initially_armed: false
    arm_rejected_while_killed: true
    applies_to: [torpedo_launcher, dropper, claw]

keys.what: IMU, FOG, DVL, depth and both stereo cameras: rate, mount and noise.
keys.summary: imu 400 Hz, fog 500 Hz, dvl 8 Hz, depth 20 Hz, ffc 15 Hz, dfc 15 Hz
keys.yaml:
# Sample times land on the 2 ms physics step.
sensors:
- id: imu
  type: ahrs
  frame: imu_mount
  mount_frame: imu_mount
  rate_hz: 400   # VN-100 as configured on Talos (2026-10-03 pool bags)
  parameters:
    inertial:
      acceleration_noise: {white_stddev: [0.035, 0.035, 0.035]}   # m/s^2, 2026-10-03 bag 01 hold
      gyro_noise: {white_stddev: [0.0009, 0.0009, 0.0009]}   # rad/s, 2026-10-03 bag 01 hold
      reporting:
        gravity_magnitude_m_s2: 9.755455    # matches EKF gravitational_acceleration; plant uses 9.80665
        force_variance: [0.01, 0.01, 0.01]
        angular_variance: [0.01, 0.01, 0.01]
    attitude:
      angle_stddev_rad: 0.0002   # VN-100 attitude is filtered, nearly noise-free (2026-10-03 bags)
      heading_drift_rad_s: 0.0
      reported_variance: [5.0e-05, 1.0e-05, 0.01]
- id: fog
  type: fog
  frame: fog_mount
  mount_frame: fog_mount
  rate_hz: 500
  parameters:
    axes: [[0, 0, 1]]

keys.what: Torpedo launcher, dropper, claw and magnet, with their physical parameters.
keys.yaml:
# Payloads, claw and magnet.
mechanisms:
- id: torpedo_launcher
  type: launcher
  frame: torpedoes_mount
  parameters:
    # Slot poses in torpedoes_mount; the nose is slot +X. Fires slot_0 then slot_1.
    slots:
    - {id: slot_0, position_m: [0.01594921, -0.02560642, -0.0218555], orientation_wxyz: [1, 0, 0, 0]}
    - {id: slot_1, position_m: [0.01594921, 0.00939685, -0.0218555], orientation_wxyz: [1, 0, 0, 0]}
    projectile:
      model: finned_rigid_body   # rotates under drag and buoyancy
      length_m: 0.08299993
      radius_m: 0.013
      mass_kg: 0.01222
      displaced_volume_m3: 1.2e-05
      added_mass_kg: 0.003
      drag_axial: 0.015
      drag_lateral: 0.35
      center_of_mass_m: 0.02         # axial, +X nose, from mesh center
      center_of_buoyancy_m: -0.02
      center_of_drag_m: -0.025
      angular_damping_n_m_s: 0.01
      neutral_buoyancy: false
      max_age_s: 30   # removed (a miss) after this long
    launch: {spring_energy_j: 0.047}   # launch speed = sqrt(2E / (mass + added mass)) + vehicle velocity

keys.what: The points tasks test for "went through the gate" or "surfaced".
keys.yaml:
# Points the tasks test for gate passes, breaching and surfacing:
# all 8 corners of every collision box, plus the magnet tip point.
scoring_envelope:
  collision_boxes: [hull_0, hull_1]
  points:
  - {id: magnet_tip, frame: magnet_mount, position_m: [0, 0, 0.05]}

label: tasks.yaml
description: RoboSub 2026 course tasks and scoring (Survey & Repair / Search & Rescue roles).

keys.what: Every mesh and texture the task files use.
The task files in this course.
keys.summary: gate, torpedo, table, slalom, bins, surface
keys.yaml: tasks: [gate.yaml, torpedo.yaml, table.yaml, slalom.yaml, bins.yaml, surface.yaml]   # task files (kind task)

keys.what: Mechanisms a robot must have for each task (checked when a scenario is resolved).
Choices made before a run: role, coin flips, pinger, the bins' vinyl classes.
Which compiled C++ rules class scores the run, and all its point values.
keys.yaml:
# Scoring: compiled rules (extensions/rules/robosub_2026) and their parameters. The rules turn
# (run state, events since the last call) into score row changes, run-status fields and the event feed.
scoring_rules:
- name: robosub_2026
  parameters:
    roles:
      repair: {target_class: fire, facing_icons: [compass, hammer_and_wrench]}
      rescue: {target_class: blood, facing_icons: [buoy, sos]}
    award_policy: max_per_row   # a row's score only increases
    eligibility: gate_passed_and_not_ended   # every row but the gate needs the gate passed first
    gate:
      role_reference_frame: gate_repair   # repair iff the crossing is on this frame's side
      style: {quarter_rad: 1.5707963267948966, epsilon_rad: 1.0e-6, max_quarters: 8, roll_pitch_first: true}
    torpedo:
      good_results: [success, wrong_target]   # both count for per-shot points
      sequence_order: [large, small]   # launch order, both at the correct class
      release_distance: {task: torpedo, measure: abs_local_x_of_projectile_tip}
    points:   # RoboSub 2026 points
      pinger_first: 500
      pinger_second: 1500
      gate: 100
      heading: 300
      role: 150
      slalom_same: 400
      slalom_other: 200
      slalom_depth: 200

keys.what: The rows of the scorecard, in order.
Counters shown per task: success, wrong target, blocked, miss.
keys.yaml:
# Payload/claw outcome counters published on simulator/task_score.
outcome_counters: [success, wrong_target, blocked, miss]

keys.what: Operator messages at start and stop.
keys.yaml:
run_messages:
  start: "Run started; pass the gate first"
  stop: Run stopped
  adjustment: Manual adjustment updated
  reset: Tasks and run reset

keys.what: How the viewer shows the run: labels, status fields, focus list.
keys.summary: title, run_options, focus, demo_targets, manual_adjustment … (11 keys)

label: gate
description: Start gate with role halves; forward pass and reverse (return-home) pass.

keys.what: Named points on the prop (what mapping estimates, where the tree aims).
keys.yaml:
# Role halves.
frames:
- {id: gate_repair, position_m: [0.0, -0.75, 0.5], orientation_wxyz: [1, 0, 0, 0]}   # repair = local -Y
- {id: gate_rescue, position_m: [0.0, 0.75, 0.5], orientation_wxyz: [1, 0, 0, 0]}

keys.what: Physical things: static structures and loose objects the claw can pick up.
Judged volumes: a gate opening, torpedo holes, a bin, a magnet target.
keys.yaml:
regions:
- id: gate_opening
  type: rectangular_portal
  parameters:
    plane: {axis: x, offset_m: 0.0}
    # A pass counts when every scoring_envelope point is inside these bounds (gate frame).
    bounds_local: {abs_y_lt_m: 1.5, z_lt_m: 0.75}   # half width, top of the opening
    world_floor_clearance: true                    # every envelope vertex above the pool floor
    crossing_reference: robot_reference_origin     # interpolated sign change of reference-origin local x
    fit_checks: [envelope_at_crossing_point_with_current_orientation, envelope_at_completion]
    traversal: full_envelope                       # side counts only when all vertices share it
    approach_radius_m: 3.0                         # attempt opens/closes here (style tracking)
    max_pose_step_m: 2.0                           # larger reference-origin jump resets the judge

keys.what: What the runtime reports: passes, hits, drops, contacts.
Per-task scoring hooks (the RoboSub rules do the scoring).
keys.yaml:
# Gate and return-home points depend on role, coin flips and style: scored by the rules.
scoring: []

label: slalom
description: Three slalom rows crossed on the reference origin; side and depth are scored by the rules.

keys.what: Named points on the prop (what mapping estimates, where the tree aims).
Physical things: static structures and loose objects the claw can pick up.
Judged volumes: a gate opening, torpedo holes, a bin, a magnet target.
keys.yaml:
# Each row is a portal in its own frame. Only the reference-origin crossing point counts:
# 0 < |y| < 1.55 (side = sign(y)); depth_overlap uses the envelope's conservative vertical extent
# against the z band. Rows score only positive -> negative crossings.
regions:
- id: slalom_front
  type: rectangular_portal
  parameters:
    frame: slalom_front
    plane: {axis: x, offset_m: 0.0}
    bounds_local: {abs_y_lt_m: 1.55, z_lt_m: 0.474}   # half width; z_lt_m is not used by this fit check
    world_floor_clearance: false
    crossing_reference: robot_reference_origin
    fit_checks: [reference_origin_at_crossing]
    traversal: reference_origin
    depth_band_m: [-0.81, 0.474]   # bottom, top
    approach_radius_m: 3.0
    max_pose_step_m: 2.0
- id: slalom_middle
  type: rectangular_portal
  parameters:
    frame: slalom_middle
    plane: {axis: x, offset_m: 0.0}
    bounds_local: {abs_y_lt_m: 1.55, z_lt_m: 0.474}   # half width; z_lt_m is not used by this fit check
    world_floor_clearance: false
    crossing_reference: robot_reference_origin
    fit_checks: [reference_origin_at_crossing]

keys.what: What the runtime reports: passes, hits, drops, contacts.
Per-task scoring hooks (the RoboSub rules do the scoring).
keys.yaml: scoring: []   # same-side/other-side and depth points depend on the gate side: scored by the rules

    # basket walls.

    - {id: slab, size_m: [0.635, 0.635, 0.01905], center_m: [0, 0, -0.009525], orientation_wxyz: [1, 0, 0, 0]}
    visuals:   # table and basket meshes (origins match the collision meshes)
    - {asset: table_visual, frame: task, position_m: [0, 0, 0], orientation_wxyz: [1, 0, 0, 0]}
    - {asset: basket_helmet_visual, frame: helmet_basket, position_m: [0, 0, 0], orientation_wxyz: [1, 0, 0, 0]}
    - {asset: basket_warning_visual, frame: warning_basket, position_m: [0, 0, 0], orientation_wxyz: [1, 0, 0, 0]}
    collision_meshes:
    - {id: table, asset: table_mesh, frame: task, lateral_friction: 0.7, restitution: 0.05}
    - {id: helmet_basket, asset: basket_helmet_mesh, frame: helmet_basket, lateral_friction: 0.7, restitution: 0.05}
    - {id: warning_basket, asset: basket_warning_mesh, frame: warning_basket, lateral_friction: 0.7, restitution: 0.05}
- id: pill
  type: rigid_body
  parameters:
    frame: pill
    collision_asset: pill_mesh
    visual_asset: pill_visual

    expected_region: helmet_basket

label: parts.yaml
description: Named pieces of the RoboSub 2026 course artwork and props, for labeled renders.

keys.what: Pixel maps that name each piece of the printed artwork (fire, blood, rings).
keys.yaml:
# Part maps: 8-bit grayscale PNGs, same size and UV layout as the texture; pixel value -> part.
# Built by tools/generate_part_masks.py (re-run it after editing a seed or a texture; the test checks
# the committed PNGs are current). Each part is its whole emoji silhouette, holes filled: a seed is a
# pixel on the emoji (texture px, top-left origin). Optional keys: threshold (max channel distance
# from the background color, default 24/255; 40 cuts the soft glow some emojis carry, 4-6 keeps
# near-white highlights that reach the edge), close_px (default 2), background ([r, g, b]) and fill:
#   small  (default) fill holes under 15 % of the component area: letters, windows, the compass hook
#          loop; larger enclosed background (the helmet strap loop) stays background
#   all    fill every hole: rings (ring + hole disk) and the buoy (its white center)
#   none   no fill
textures:
# Torpedo board. Rings: the four red rings, each covering ring + hole disk (the hole itself is a real
# cutout). Values follow the panel holes in torpedo.yaml (center px = (u, 1 - v) * 2304).
- texture: torpedo_texture
  mask: assets/torpedo/Task4_ver1_parts.png
  parts:
  - {value: 1, part: icon_fire, seed_px: [376, 378], threshold: 40}   # soft glow on the left edge
  - {value: 2, part: icon_blood, seed_px: [1979, 1404]}
  - {value: 3, part: icon_ambulance, seed_px: [507, 1916], threshold: 6}   # pale highlights reach the edge
  - {value: 4, part: icon_fire_engine, seed_px: [1839, 464], threshold: 6}
  - {value: 5, part: ring, seed_px: [372, 679], fill: all}     # fire_large
  - {value: 6, part: ring, seed_px: [1184, 213], fill: all}    # fire_small
  - {value: 7, part: ring, seed_px: [1970, 1700], fill: all}   # blood_large
  - {value: 8, part: ring, seed_px: [1153, 1652], fill: all}   # blood_small

# Gate role halves.

label: uwrt_talos
description: Talos <-> UWRT robot stack (controller, EKF, acoustics, perception, autonomy).

keys.what: Refuses to run with any other robot pack.
keys.yaml: requires_robot: talos   # binds to the robot pack's ids

keys.what: Prefix for every relative topic and service: /talos.
keys.yaml: namespace: /talos   # relative names resolve here (the controller hardcodes /talos)

keys.what: The ROS node the simulator appears as.
keys.yaml: node_name: physics_simulator   # hosts the real_time_factor parameter

keys.what: Simulator frame name to ROS frame name.
keys.summary: world, imu_mount, fog_mount, dvl_mount, ffc_mount … (10 keys)
keys.yaml:
# Simulator frame id -> ROS frame name. Only frames used in headers/TF are listed. The simulator world is the
# stack's fixed `world` frame (world->odom is static), not `map`: a mapping calibration moves world->map, and truth
# must stay where the pool is.
frame_names:
  world: world
  imu_mount: talos/imu_link
  fog_mount: talos/fog_link
  dvl_mount: talos/dvl_link
  ffc_mount: talos/ffc_camera_link
  dfc_mount: talos/dfc_camera_link
  ffc_left_optical: talos/ffc_left_camera_optical_frame
  ffc_right_optical: talos/ffc_right_camera_optical_frame
  dfc_left_optical: talos/dfc_left_camera_optical_frame
  dfc_right_optical: talos/dfc_right_camera_optical_frame

keys.what: /clock: 500 Hz, starting at the wall-clock time, never rewinding.
keys.summary: topic, epoch, rate_hz, reset_policy, real_time_factor … (6 keys)
keys.yaml:
clock:
  topic: /clock                          # rosgraph_msgs/msg/Clock
  epoch: system_time_at_start   # starts at system time, so ROS time is never 0
  rate_hz: 500   # every 2 ms physics step
  reset_policy: preserve_ros_epoch_and_time   # ROS time never rewinds across resets
  real_time_factor: 1.0
  qos: {history: keep_last, depth: 10, reliability: reliable, durability: volatile}

keys.what: Maps the controller's 8-float force array onto the robot pack's thrusters.
keys.yaml:
thrusters:
  order: [VUS, VUP, HUS, HUP, HLS, HLP, VLS, VLP]   # thruster index 0..7 of the controller's wrench matrix
  input_scales: [1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1]
  reject: [wrong_length, nonfinite]   # the whole message is ignored

keys.what: Which TF frames the simulator publishes, which it only reads, and which it must never publish.
Which streams carry the kill command and the kill state.
keys.yaml:
kill:
  command_stream: software_kill
  state_stream: firmware_kill

keys.what: Service names for the three kinds of reset.
keys.yaml:
reset:
  robot_service: reset_sim_to_start      # plant to start pose; tasks untouched
  tasks_service: reset_tasks             # tasks + reload + disarm
  full_service: reset_scenario   # whole scenario

keys.what: Services that move the simulated robot, and how the EKF is told about it.
keys.yaml:
placement:
  set_service: set_sim_pose
  sync_service: sync_sim_to_estimate
  estimator_alignment:   # never during a run
    client: /talos/set_pose
    service_type: robot_localization/srv/SetPose
    triggers: [startup, placement, reset_to_start, full_reset]
    estimate_stream: ekf_odometry        # header.frame_id gives the EKF frame; world->it via tf.lookup
    pose: reference_frame                # robot reference_frame (base_link)
    covariance_diagonal: 1.0e-06

keys.what: One entry per topic: direction, ROS type, simulator endpoint, rate and field mapping.
keys.yaml:
streams:
# ---------------- ROS -> simulator ----------------
- id: thruster_forces
  direction: subscribe
  topic: thruster_forces                 # controller publishes /talos/thruster_forces
  message_type: std_msgs/msg/Float32MultiArray
  native: 'command:thrusters.set_forces'
  frame_id: ''
  rate_hz: 0
  qos: {history: keep_last, depth: 10, reliability: reliable, durability: volatile}
  fields: {forces_n: {from: data}}
- id: software_kill
  direction: subscribe
  topic: command/software_kill
  message_type: riptide_msgs2/msg/KillSwitchReport
  native: 'command:robot.set_killed'
  frame_id: ''
  rate_hz: 0
  qos: {history: keep_last, depth: 10, reliability: reliable, durability: volatile}
  accept_if: [{field: kill_switch_id, equals: 1}]   # KILL_SWITCH_RQT_CONTROLLER only
  fields: {killed: {from: switch_asserting_kill}}
- id: ekf_odometry
  direction: subscribe
  topic: odometry/filtered
  message_type: nav_msgs/msg/Odometry
  native: 'estimate:latest'              # bridge-held sample for sync_sim_to_estimate / alignment

keys.what: ROS services the simulator offers: reset, place, arm, fire, claw.
Custom message converters (none needed for Talos).
keys.yaml: converters: []

tasks:

    count: 400

              aim_jitter_deg: 20, roll_deg: 4, pitch_deg: 6}
  torpedo:
    count: 500
    sampler: {type: approach, frame: task, facing: [1, 0, 0], range_m: [0.8, 4.5], bearing_deg: 50,
              elevation_deg: [-10, 20], aim_jitter_deg: 12, roll_deg: 4, pitch_deg: 6}
  surface:
    count: 400
    # From inside the octagon, below the signs (surfacing).
    sampler: {type: approach, frame: [compass, hammer_and_wrench, buoy, sos], facing: [1, 0, 0],
              range_m: [0.6, 2.6], bearing_deg: 50, elevation_deg: [-35, 5], aim_jitter_deg: 12,
              roll_deg: 4, pitch_deg: 8}
  bins:
    count: 300

    sampler: {type: approach, frame: [magnet_target1, magnet_target2], facing: [1, 0, 0], range_m: [0.5, 2.0],

keys.what: Water, lighting and image effects, varied per image, grouped in named looks.
keys.yaml:
# Appearance. Water is relative to the pool pack's calibrated optics (robosub_2026: scattering 0.458), so
# scale 1 is the pool as calibrated. RoboSub is outdoors: mostly the nominal look, some clear bright midday,
# some murky water, a little overcast.
randomize:
  placement: {groups: [[surface, table]]}   # the octagon hangs over the table: jitter them together
  environments:
    list:
    - id: nominal
      weight: 5
      water: {scattering_scale: [0.85, 1.2], absorption_scale: [0.85, 1.2]}
    - id: clear
      weight: 2
      water: {scattering_scale: [0.55, 0.8], absorption_scale: [0.7, 0.9]}
      # Exposure capped at 1.15: brighter washes out the white table top seen by dfc.
      lighting: {caustics: [0.8, 1.5], exposure: [0.9, 1.15], direct_light_scale: [1.0, 1.2],
                 sun_elevation_deg: [60, 85]}
    - id: murky
      weight: 2
      # Scattering x1.7 already hides a board 4 m away and x2.2 makes it nearly invisible: stay near the
      # edge of the label range, not past it.
      water: {scattering_scale: [1.3, 1.8], absorption_scale: [1.2, 1.6]}
      # Turbid water dims the sun: with the default direct light (up to x1.2) murky:max read washed out.
      lighting: {caustics: [0.0, 0.4], exposure: [0.8, 1.0], direct_light_scale: [0.7, 1.0]}
      image: {noise_sigma: [1, 5], blur_px: [0.3, 1.2]}
    - id: overcast
      weight: 1
